specAnchors.text: explain ways of reducing unwanted energy transfer, such as insulation

primer.text: Most wasted energy escapes by heating, so cutting waste means cutting conduction and convection. This note assembles the toolkit — low-conductivity insulators, immobilised fluids, thickness — and applies it where houses need it: fibreglass in the loft and insulation in the cavity walls.

modules.title: Reducing unwanted energy transfers
modules.opening: Wasted energy mostly leaves by heating, so the fight against waste is a fight against conduction and convection. Low-conductivity materials block the first, preventing fluid movement blocks the second, and insulation — loft fibreglass, cavity wall fill — applies both ideas where a house loses most.
keyPoints: Energy dissipated to the surroundings is the main source of wasted energy transfers.
Conduction is reduced by using materials with low thermal conductivity — insulators.
Convection is reduced by preventing the fluid that forms the currents from moving.
An insulator’s effectiveness depends on its thermal conductivity (lower is better), its density (more dense conducts more) and its thickness (thicker insulates better).
Loft insulation (fibreglass) and cavity wall insulation lower a house’s rate of cooling.

low.restatement: Stop conduction with poor conductors, stop convection by immobilising the fluid, and buy thickness: insulation is those three rules applied to lofts and wall cavities.
low.analogy: Dressing for snow: a thick coat of low-conductivity fabric with still air trapped inside is a wearable insulation panel.
low.examPointer: The three effectiveness factors — conductivity, density, thickness — with their directions (lower, lower, higher) are the examinable list.

medium.restatement: Houses lose energy fastest where large warm surfaces meet moving cold air; fibreglass lofts trap still air above, and cavity wall fill turns the gap between two wall layers into a low-conductivity barrier.
medium.analogy: Two doors against the draught: the loft lid closes the top exit, the cavity fill plugs the wall’s hollow middle.
medium.examPointer: Link insulation to money and emissions when asked why: less wasted energy means lower bills and fewer greenhouse gases from the saved heating.

glossary.definition: A material with low thermal conductivity that reduces energy transfer by conduction.
Insulating material filling the gap between a house’s external wall layers.
A reinforced plastic of woven material and glass fibres; trapped air between the fibres makes it a good insulator.
How quickly a object transfers energy to its surroundings; insulation lowers it.
